local View = {}

local function fontFace(weight)
	return Font.new("rbxasset://fonts/families/Montserrat.json", weight, Enum.FontStyle.Normal)
end

local function applyShadow(guiObject)
	local ok, shadow = pcall(Instance.new, "UIShadow")
	if ok then
		shadow.Name = "Shadow"
		shadow.Color = Color3.fromRGB(4, 10, 20)
		shadow.Transparency = 0.42
		shadow.BlurRadius = UDim.new(0, 20)
		shadow.Offset = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 8)
		shadow.Parent = guiObject
		return shadow
	end
	return nil
end

local function makeCorner(parent, radius)
	local c = Instance.new("UICorner")
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, radius)
	c.Parent = parent
	return c
end

local function makeStroke(parent, color, thickness, transparency)
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
	s.Color = color
	s.Thickness = thickness or 1
	s.Transparency = transparency or 0
	s.Parent = parent
	return s
end

local function makeGradient(parent, rotation, colors, transparency)
	local g = Instance.new("UIGradient")
	g.Rotation = rotation or 90
	g.Color = colors
	if transparency then
		g.Transparency = transparency
	end
	g.Parent = parent
	return g
end

local function createTextLabel(name, parent, text, size, weight, color, transparency)
	local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	label.Name = name
	label.BackgroundTransparency = transparency == nil and 1 or transparency
	label.BorderSizePixel = 0
	label.Text = text
	label.TextColor3 = color
	label.TextTransparency = 0
	label.TextScaled = false
	label.TextWrapped = true
	label.RichText = false
	label.FontFace = fontFace(weight)
	label.TextSize = size
	label.ZIndex = 10
	label.Parent = parent
	return label
end

local function createIcon(name, parent, image, size, anchorPoint, position)
	local icon = Instance.new("ImageLabel")
	icon.Name = name
	icon.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	icon.BorderSizePixel = 0
	icon.Image = image
	icon.ImageColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	icon.ScaleType = Enum.ScaleType.Fit
	icon.Size = size
	icon.AnchorPoint = anchorPoint or Vector2.new(0, 0.5)
	icon.Position = position or UDim2.new(0, 0, 0.5, 0)
	icon.ZIndex = 12
	icon.Parent = parent
	return icon
end

local function setModalVisible(modal, visible)
	local panel = getPanel(modal)
	if not panel then
		modal.Visible = visible
		if modal:IsA("CanvasGroup") then
			modal.GroupTransparency = visible and 0 or 1
		end
		return
	end

	cancelModalTween(modal)
	local scale = ensurePanelScale(panel)

	if visible then
		modal.Visible = true
		if modal:IsA("CanvasGroup") then
			modal.GroupTransparency = 1
		end
		scale.Scale = 0.96

		local tween = TweenService:Create(
			modal,
			TweenInfo.new(0.22, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
			{ GroupTransparency = 0 }
		)
		local scaleTween = TweenService:Create(
			scale,
			TweenInfo.new(0.22, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
			{ Scale = 1 }
		)
		modalTweens[modal] = tween
		tween:Play()
		scaleTween:Play()
	else
		local tween = TweenService:Create(
			modal,
			TweenInfo.new(0.16, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.In),
			{ GroupTransparency = 1 }
		)
		local scaleTween = TweenService:Create(

			{ Scale = 0.96 }
		)

		scaleTween:Play()
		addCleanup(tween.Completed:Connect(function()
			if modal.GroupTransparency >= 0.99 then

function Responsive.bind(root)

    local function update()
        local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
        if not camera then return end
        local size = camera.ViewportSize
        local mobile = math.min(size.X, size.Y) < 600
        for _, node in root:GetDescendants() do
            if node:IsA("GuiObject") then
                if node.Name == "_NexusDesktop" then node.Visible = not mobile end
                if node.Name == "_NexusMobile" then node.Visible = mobile end
            end
        end
    end
    local function observeCamera()
        if cameraConnection then cameraConnection:Disconnect() end
        local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
        if camera then cameraConnection = camera:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"):Connect(update) end
        update()
    end
    table.insert(connections, workspace:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CurrentCamera"):Connect(observeCamera))
    local function cleanup()
        if cameraConnection then cameraConnection:Disconnect() end
        for _, connection in connections do connection:Disconnect() end
        table.clear(connections)
    end
    table.insert(connections, root.Destroying:Connect(cleanup))
    observeCamera()
    return cleanup
end

    button.AutoButtonColor = false
    local controller = {}
    bound[button] = controller
    local previousState = nil
    local hoverScale = math.clamp(tonumber(options.hoverScale) or 1.05, 1, 1.1)
    local pressScale = math.clamp(tonumber(options.pressScale) or 0.95, 0.85, 1)
    local duration = math.clamp(tonumber(options.duration) or 0.12, 0.06, 0.3)
    local shadow = options.shadow
    local shadowPosition = shadow and shadow.Position

    local function soundFor(kind, soundId)
        if type(soundId) ~= "string" or not soundId:match("^rbxassetid://%d+$") then return end
        local sound = Instance.new("Sound")
        sound.Name = "Feedback_" .. kind
        sound.SoundId = soundId
        sound.Volume = math.clamp(tonumber(options.volume) or 0.18, 0, 0.35)
        sound.Parent = button
        sounds[kind] = sound
    end
    soundFor("hover", options.hoverSound)
    soundFor("click", options.clickSound)

    local function playSound(kind)
        if not alive or not button.Interactable or options.sounds == false then return end
        local sound = sounds[kind]
        local now = os.clock()
        local delay = kind == "hover" and 0.12 or 0.08
        if not sound or now - lastSoundAt[kind] < delay then return end
        lastSoundAt[kind] = now
        sound.TimePosition = 0
        sound:Play()
    end

    local function pointerAvailable()
        return UserInputService.MouseEnabled
            and UserInputService:GetLastInputType() ~= Enum.UserInputType.Touch
    end

    local function refresh()
        if not alive then return end
        local state = button.GuiState
        local target = 1
        if button.Interactable then
            if state == Enum.GuiState.Press then
                target = pressScale
            elseif (state == Enum.GuiState.Hover and pointerAvailable() and options.hoverEnabled ~= false) or focused then
                target = hoverScale
            end
        end
        if state == Enum.GuiState.Hover and previousState ~= state and pointerAvailable() and options.hoverEnabled ~= false then
            playSound("hover")
        end
        previousState = state
        if currentTween then
            currentTween:Cancel()
            currentTween = nil
        end
        if shadowTween then shadowTween:Cancel() end
        if GuiService.ReducedMotionEnabled or options.animations == false then
            scale.Scale = 1
            if shadow then shadow.Position = shadowPosition end
            return
        end
        currentTween = TweenService:Create(scale,
            TweenInfo.new(duration, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
            { Scale = target })
        currentTween:Play()
        if shadow then
            local offset = state == Enum.GuiState.Press and -2 or 0
            shadowTween = TweenService:Create(shadow, TweenInfo.new(duration),
                { Position = shadowPosition + UDim2.fromOffset(0, offset) })
            shadowTween:Play()
        end
    end

    connections[#connections + 1] = button
        :GetPropertyChangedSignal("GuiState"):Connect(refresh)
    connections[#connections + 1] = button
        :GetPropertyChangedSignal("Interactable"):Connect(refresh)
    connections[#connections + 1] = button.SelectionGained:Connect(function()
        focused = true
        refresh()
    end)
    connections[#connections + 1] = button.SelectionLost:Connect(function()
        focused = false
        refresh()
    end)
    connections[#connections + 1] = GuiService
        :GetPropertyChangedSignal("ReducedMotionEnabled"):Connect(refresh)
    connections[#connections + 1] = button.Activated:Connect(function()
        playSound("click")
    end)

    function controller:Destroy()
        if not alive then return end
        alive = false
        if currentTween then currentTween:Cancel() end
        if shadowTween then shadowTween:Cancel() end
        for _, connection in ipairs(connections) do connection:Disconnect() end
        for _, sound in pairs(sounds) do sound:Destroy() end
        bound[button] = nil
        scale:Destroy()
        pcall(function() button.AutoButtonColor = originalAutoColor end)
        if shadow then pcall(function() shadow.Position = shadowPosition end) end
    end
    connections[#connections + 1] = button.Destroying:Connect(function()
        controller:Destroy()
    end)
    refresh()
    return controller
end

designPlan.artDirection: A premium fantasy-sci-fi menu built around a luminous cyan-to-cobalt gloss framed by thick deep-navy structure and restrained warm gold trim. The composition avoids a full outer panel so the screen feels open, with a native dark background field, subtle radial glow, and corner ornaments that gently frame rather than dominate. A large ornamental title plate crowns the menu and establishes the AURORA identity. The Play action is unmistakably dominant through larger scale, brighter cyan highlight, and centered placement, while Settings and Credits are grouped beneath in a coherent secondary stack. Settings and Credits open matching modal panels using the same glossy skin family and gold-corner detailing. Text remains live, bright, and highly legible against darker surfaces. Slider and toggle behavior remain native Roblox controls, visually styled with matching cyan, cobalt, navy, and gold surfaces; the artwork need is limited to shared skins and icons while tracks, fills, and state transitions are composed with native UI objects. Decorative energy is concentrated near the title plate and corners, leaving the center readable and action-focused.

composition.focalPoint: The eye lands first on the AURORA title plate at upper center, then immediately drops to an oversized Play button centered in the main vertical stack. Settings and Credits sit directly below as a smaller matching pair to maintain one connected action column. Modal panels appear centered above the menu with settings slightly larger and credits compact, both sharing the same skin family and close placement in the upper-right of each panel for immediate comprehension.
composition.alignmentSystem: Strict vertical center alignment for the main menu stack on desktop and mobile, with symmetrical ornament framing. Title plate, dock, and modal panels share a central axis. Internal panel content uses left-aligned labels with right-aligned controls for settings rows. Close buttons anchor to panel top-right corners. Repeated edge insets, equal button widths within groups, and consistent top-to-bottom rhythm preserve coherence across breakpoints.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Cyan and cobalt provide the rich glossy identity, navy supplies the thick structural edge and depth, and gold is reserved for trim, icon glints, and title emphasis so it feels premium rather than noisy. Dark neutral background values keep the bright interface readable and prevent ornamentation from overpowering action controls. Settings controls inherit the same palette to stay unified rather than introducing new system colors.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Heavy navy outer stroke for skinned buttons and panels, supported by slimmer inner cyan or gold highlight lines on hero elements. Native controls use 2-3px equivalent strokes with rounded ends and gold micro-accents only at focus points.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Short, dense navy-black shadows with a soft downward offset for foreground separation, plus subtle cyan bloom on primary surfaces. The effect is glossy and dimensional without cartoon bounce.

designPlan.artDirection: A premium fantasy-sci-fi menu built around a luminous cyan-to-cobalt gloss framed by thick deep-navy structure and restrained warm gold trim. The composition avoids a full outer panel so the screen feels open, with a native dark background field, subtle radial glow, and corner ornaments that gently frame rather than dominate. A large ornamental title plate crowns the menu and establishes the AURORA identity. The Play action is unmistakably dominant through larger scale, brighter cyan highlight, and centered placement, while Settings and Credits are grouped beneath in a coherent secondary stack. Settings and Credits open matching modal panels using the same glossy skin family and gold-corner detailing. Text remains live, bright, and highly legible against darker surfaces. Slider and toggle behavior remain native Roblox controls, visually styled with matching cyan, cobalt, navy, and gold surfaces; the artwork need is limited to shared skins and icons while tracks, fills, and state transitions are composed with native UI objects. Decorative energy is concentrated near the title plate and corners, leaving the center readable and action-focused.

composition.focalPoint: The eye lands first on the AURORA title plate at upper center, then immediately drops to an oversized Play button centered in the main vertical stack. Settings and Credits sit directly below as a smaller matching pair to maintain one connected action column. Modal panels appear centered above the menu with settings slightly larger and credits compact, both sharing the same skin family and close placement in the upper-right of each panel for immediate comprehension.
composition.alignmentSystem: Strict vertical center alignment for the main menu stack on desktop and mobile, with symmetrical ornament framing. Title plate, dock, and modal panels share a central axis. Internal panel content uses left-aligned labels with right-aligned controls for settings rows. Close buttons anchor to panel top-right corners. Repeated edge insets, equal button widths within groups, and consistent top-to-bottom rhythm preserve coherence across breakpoints.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Cyan and cobalt provide the rich glossy identity, navy supplies the thick structural edge and depth, and gold is reserved for trim, icon glints, and title emphasis so it feels premium rather than noisy. Dark neutral background values keep the bright interface readable and prevent ornamentation from overpowering action controls. Settings controls inherit the same palette to stay unified rather than introducing new system colors.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Heavy navy outer stroke for skinned buttons and panels, supported by slimmer inner cyan or gold highlight lines on hero elements. Native controls use 2-3px equivalent strokes with rounded ends and gold micro-accents only at focus points.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Short, dense navy-black shadows with a soft downward offset for foreground separation, plus subtle cyan bloom on primary surfaces. The effect is glossy and dimensional without cartoon bounce.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build a centered ceremonial composition with generous side breathing room. Title plate and primary action stack occupy the visual spine. Settings and credits modals appear centered above the menu without shifting the background layout. Desktop preserves more ornament visibility and slightly wider panels, with left-right alignment inside settings rows.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Use _NexusMobile with the same node names under a separate mobile frame tree. Simplify background ornament spread, widen the action stack, enlarge button heights, and reduce title plate height. Settings panel becomes wider with more vertical row spacing and may reflow the volume label/value around the slider for finger comfort. Modal margins must respect notches and home indicators. No hover behaviors are synthesized; only touch feedback and drag interactions are used.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Tablet keeps the centered composition but interpolates between desktop spaciousness and mobile touch sizing. Main menu width sits between the two, ornaments remain visible but restrained, and settings rows can stay horizontal unless viewport becomes narrow. Panels remain centrally overlaid with desktop-like proportions and mobile-safe touch targets.

implementationNotes: Create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile root groups at View.build() return, each containing the same canonical node names from the library template; desktop visible initially.

Use the exact supported node names: BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, SettingsTitle, SettingsCloseButton, MusicRow, MusicLabel, MusicToggle, VolumeRow, VolumeLabel, VolumeSlider, VolumeValue, CreditsModal, CreditsTitle, CreditsBody, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
Do not add SettingsSeparator because it is optional and unnecessary for this composition.
MainMenuDock should remain transparent; do not introduce an outer menu panel or extra navigation.
TitlePlate, primary/secondary button skins, close button skin, and modal panel skins should each be requested as reusable shared artwork families, not many near-identical variants.
BackgroundRoot must be native Roblox layout and gradients; keep decoration restrained and do not use a full illustrated scene.

Despite asset request wording, slider track/fill/handle and toggle housing/thumb/state visuals must be built natively with Frames, UICorner, UIStroke, and UIGradient. Use the Gemini skin language as color/material reference rather than separate generated state pieces.
Keep all labels and dynamic values as live Roblox text; do not bake AURORA, button labels, settings labels, or credits text into images.
Implement panel visibility and exclusivity in PanelControllerBehavior: opening Settings hides Credits, opening Credits hides Settings, and both close buttons hide only their respective panel.

PlayButton Activated must hide the menu root and call a clearly named local hook through OnPlayRequestedHook, such as firing a BindableEvent or invoking a callback named OnPlayRequested; keep this local only.
Runtime should switch to the mobile frame group when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) < 600, without waiting on controller construction.
Use local helper functions inside View for repeated skin, stroke, padding, and text setup; place runtime hover/press logic in a shared ButtonEffects module.
All actionable controls must meet minimum touch targets: Play 56, secondary menu buttons 52, close buttons 44, toggle 44, slider interaction band 44.
CreditsBody should be concise placeholder live text only if actual credit content is unavailable, and remain easy to replace without layout breakage.
Use UIScale and UITextSizeConstraint to preserve readability across desktop, tablet, and phone portrait rather than uniformly scaling the whole tree.
Initial modal instances must exist at build time and start hidden via Visible/CanvasGroup state so the preview adapter can verify them.
Keep icon treatment fully consistent across Play, Settings, Credits, and both Close buttons using the shared aurora_gemini family.
